iconicAnchor.label: Musica Viva, 1958
iconicAnchor.whyCanonical: Its asymmetric grid, mathematical rhythm, reduced sans typography, and disciplined contrast establish the style as a complete information system.

sources.title: Musica Viva
supports: Müller-Brockmann used geometric rhythm and reduced means in a canonical Swiss poster.
The poster supports the node's asymmetric grid and high-control hierarchy.

sources.title: Josef Müller-Brockmann
supports: MoMA's holdings show the grammar applied across concert, exhibition, safety, and cultural posters.
The breadth supports treating this as a repeatable system rather than one poster effect.

bundledReferenceRationale: Excellent single-image set. The lead clearly teaches grid, flush left, asymmetric, objective photography, retains its identity at card scale, and shows no visible anti-cue, integrity failure, or confusing overlap with neighboring styles. The independently approved lead is assets/refs/international-typographic-style/generated-lead.jpg. No support image is needed because the lead carries the direction without filler.
